To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the late-orogenic granitoids in southern Finland were emplaced in a transpressional setting; and (ii) the late-orogeny granites were emplaced as small batches of chemically variable melts, which were fractionated and collected at different levels in the crust.

the great volumes (ca. 100 000 km ^{3} ) of late-orogenic granite–migmatite complexes in southern Finland were emplaced as small batches that were collected at different levels in the crust and that were subsequently deformed and fractionated during their transport and emplacement.
the late-orogenic granitic sheets in southern Finland are emplaced as small batches of melts, which are transported along channels, and which freeze at different depths in the crust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emplacement mechanisms of late orogenic granites.
the processes that lead to the emplacement of large granitic bodies, and the role of shear in this process.
the emplacement mechanisms of late orogenic granites and the role of deformation in the fractionation of granitic melts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the late-orogenic granitoids and migmatites of southern Finland are a result of a large-scale transpressional tetrachronism.
the LSGM-zone granites are emplaced as small batches of melts that are collected at a certain level in the crust and that are fractionated during the emplacement process.
late-orogenic granitoids were emplaced by a combination of magmatic fractionation processes and tectonic processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the late-orogenic granitic magmas of southern Finland were emplaced in the middle crust as a result of crustal thickening, and that the emplacement was facilitated by repeated ductile shearing and fractionation processes.
the late-orogenic granitoids were emplaced in a transpressional regime and the fractionation of these granitoids was enhanced by the shearing of the granites.
the LSGM granites were transported in a transpressional regime and collected at a certain level in the crust, and that fractionation processes were active during transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the late-orogenic granitic magmas in southern Finland were emplaced as small batches of melt that were collected at different levels of the crust and that the granites were emplaced in a transpressive tectonic setting.
the LSGM-zone granites and migmasites are the result of a complex interplay between tectonic movements, partial melting and melt transport.
the late-orogenic granitic rocks in southern Finland are a product of repeated extraction and emplacement of chemically variable batches of melts from the crust.
